what: The focused launcher run compiled and passed all new constructor, environment, cleanup and real ELF controls, but three existing stub-wait tests failed when selecting Direct after another test had already used the process-wide Ring driver. The first panic poisoned their private Once and caused the other two failures.
cost: The focused launcher receipt ended 101 with 135 tests passed and three failed, despite the seven real native-load and five native-load-core controls passing.
cause: Stub-wait tests initialized a process-global driver inside their own private helper. Other native tests could enter a kernel wait first, so parallel test order decided which driver froze. Separate child-process runners also duplicated environment reads and cleanup paths.
class: independent native test fixtures configure shared process state
prevention: One cfg(test) driver chooses Direct once before kernel-waiting setup, owns scoped-thread startup, and dispatches typed signal and argument cases through one bounded child-process runner. Run the complete launcher library with the real ELF integration tests together, retaining allocation-free stub, signal, constructor, environment/atexit and omitted-stop controls. Keep test modules in the established test-file naming convention so fixture variables are not classified as user settings.
workaround: None. No test is skipped or serialized, and no test, cast, or ambient-effect ceiling is increased.
fix: The shared driver and consolidated controls passed on exact tree 82cc34a97458a3c996a3870546d6cb990386d921: 125 launcher library tests, five native-library tests and seven real native-loader tests, with no failures. All three previously failing stub-wait tests and the real signal, argument, environment/atexit and cleanup controls executed. The gate confirms no added launcher std, cast or ambient-effect violations and one fewer allocation signature, from removing the duplicate signal process runner; the canonical allocation row is lowered from 36 to 35. The separate stop-classification finding remains visible for correction.
